mapping.original: TryGetCurrent reads native thread-local isolate; InContext separately checks the entered context.
mapping.port: The immediate synchronous native ABI supplies its actual borrowed caller JSContext, or explicit null. This projection is never inferred from an Agent, retained Environment, or last-created VM.

mapping.original: Context Enter/Exit and current-isolate native scopes save and restore their preceding pointer.
mapping.port: C enter returns previous TLS context; leave restores it; noncopyable/nonmovable C++ Scope brackets one immediate ABI body and all its later locals. Explicit null masks an outer caller until that scope returns.

mapping.original: DumpJavaScriptBacktrace/GetCurrentStackTrace bypass JS capture when no current isolate or no context is entered.
mapping.port: Worker thread TLS starts null. Context-free native classes use the current projection only at a terminal CHECK, while all Agent/writer/buffer/task members remain free of JSContext and Engine.

mapping.original: The original trace body does not enter a new isolate or manufacture a context.
mapping.port: This adapter projects an already-entered caller, not Isolate::Enter, Context::Enter, an ownership entitlement, or a replacement for their heap allocations. It makes no VM call and cannot consume or republish pending values.

lifetime_contract: Declare DiagnosticContextScope first in every immediate synchronous tracing ABI body. Pass the actual caller context or null. It must outlive every later local/destructor/cleanup and restore before the admitted context can retire. Never copy the Scope, queue its borrowed pointer, or store it in a long-lived owner. Worker callbacks start with native TLS null; actual synchronous observer callbacks see their enclosing caller scope.
control_rationale: Live VM identity, nested same/different runtime restoration, explicit null masking, exhausted-heap/no-allocation behavior, actual ordinary/fatal/private pending preservation, C++ normal/early-return destructor order, and real worker-thread isolation are observed directly. The control helpers perform real C++ stack construction/destruction and actual native threads; they do not replace production admission.
